title: Adaptive backpressure & reservation reconciliation playbook for noisy-tenant capacity events
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: After the 2026-03-02 dedicated cluster capacity incident we observed recurrent tail-latency spikes caused by a combination of tenant reservation oversubscription, long-lived KV-cache blowups, and an overly permissive burst token policy. This ticket captures a concrete, operational playbook and engineering changes to prevent recurrence: implement a tenant-level backpressure circuit breaker, a reservation-reconciliation job (shadow reservations), and a decaying burst token bucket with per-tenant caps. The goal is to reduce eviction events and noisy-neighbor amplification while preserving short, legitimate bursts for interactive customers.

Why this differs from prior work: earlier tickets focused on static reservation tuning and eviction remediation. This design adds active reconciliation and a reactive backpressure layer that can throttle ingress early before allocations cause eviction cascades. It also introduces a short-lived 'shadow reservation' that simulates allocations to detect oversubscription without committing GPU memory. This approach allows safer, staged rollouts and faster mitigation during unknown workload surges.

Design decisions & trade-offs: 
- Backpressure circuit breaker: per-tenant adaptive window that trips based on a composite score (queue growth rate, average scheduling delay, KV cache churn). Trade-off: may increase early request latency for offending tenants but avoids global instability.
- Shadow reservations: periodically simulate reservation state changes using a non-invasive scheduler path. Trade-off: extra CPU/agent work and complexity vs earlier detection of oversubscription.
- Decaying burst tokens: tokens decay on a half-life to prevent indefinite bursting. Trade-off: small distributed token-controller state vs predictable burst budget.

High-level plan: 
1) Instrumentation (this week): add metrics for per-tenant queue growth rate, KV-cache miss+evict rates, simulated-reservation pressure, and burst-token balance. Dashboard: Grafana link below.
2) Reconciliation job (2 sprints): implement shadow reservation controller that runs every 30s to detect and surface reservation drift; create an API to propose reduced reservations for tenant owners.
3) Backpressure circuit (2 sprints, staggered rollout): implement as a middleware in the request router with a canary cluster that enforces soft-throttles before reservation allocation.
4) Burst token rework (1 sprint): switch to exponential decay model, add per-tenant hard cap and a fast-path for high-priority enterprise tenants.
5) Runbook & automation (ongoing): automated alerts, remediation playbook, and a one-click emergency quarantine in Console for fast tenant isolation.

Rollout strategy: canary on 2 non-prod clusters -> 10% of Dedicated traffic in EU region -> 25% -> global. Telemetry gates: sustained 50% reduction in eviction-rate and no customer-visible 5xx increase for 48h.

Open questions: 
- Exact scoring formula and thresholds for backpressure: start with queue-growth > 3x baseline or scheduling delay 95p > 250ms.
- Shadow reservation frequency: 30s vs 120s tradeoff between detection speed and overhead.
- Interaction with Dedicated burst-burst policy: need compatibility tests with existing burst-token bucket implementation.

Links & artifacts: 
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/DED/Shadow+Reservations+Proposal
- Grafana prototype dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/DED/capacity-telemetry-canary
- Incident postmortem: https://docs.redwood.company/postmortems/2026-03-02-dedicated-capacity-event
- Design PR (initial): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8241
- Prototype reconciler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8299

Acceptance criteria: 
- Instrumentation reports per-tenant queue-growth, KV-cache evictions, and simulated-reservation pressure for >90% of tenants.
- Shadow reconciler detects >=90% of previously-observed oversubscriptions in synthetic replay.
- Backpressure canary reduces eviction events by >=50% in a controlled run without raising customer 5xx by >1% relative.
- Burstable token decay prevents a single tenant from sustaining >200% of their baseline consumption for >10 minutes.
- Runbook published and on-call rotation trained.
